Our mission

Help Liberians build a better future through business.

Not just donations. Not just training. We want to turn skills and good ideas into real income and lasting jobs.

01 / OUR WORK

Grow your business

We help shops, hotels, and other businesses find more customers and work better.

02 / OUR WORK

Learn and earn

We help Liberians learn practical skills and gain paid work experience.

03 / OUR WORK

Start your own business

We help people with promising ideas get tools, advice, and a fair chance to begin.

These are proposed programs. Training places, grants, and jobs are not yet open or guaranteed.

Our goal is simple: help one business succeed, help one person earn, then create more opportunities.

One mission. Two ways to fund it.

Customers pay.
Supporters give.
Liberians grow.

Some businesses pay us for useful services. That money helps pay local workers and keep the work going.

Donations help fund training, equipment, and startup support for people who need a chance.

Business income helps sustain the work. Donations help more people take part.

The model

Here is how the money works.

Two sources of support. One clear purpose: jobs, skills, and stronger businesses.

Business income

A hotel pays for a website. A shop pays for stock tracking. A company pays for business support.

The money pays workers and business costs.

Donations and grants

Supporters help pay for training, work tools, paid apprenticeships, and small-business startup help.

The support opens doors for more Liberians.

What this looks like

Real problems.
Practical help.

We want to start with services people understand and businesses can use right away.

A shop wants to sell more

We build a simple website or product list so customers can find what the shop sells.

A hotel wants more bookings

We help guests find the hotel, see rooms, and contact staff easily.

A business loses track of stock

We set up a simple way to record what comes in, what sells, and what needs replacing.

A young person wants work

We teach useful skills, then connect learning with supervised, paid projects when funding allows.

For new entrepreneurs

A good idea deserves a chance.

Some people have the drive to start a business but lack basic tools or guidance.

We want to help selected entrepreneurs make a plan, find customers, and access small grants or equipment when funds are available.

Our aim is not to give money forever. It is to help a business become strong enough to stand on its own.

How we start

Start small.
Show results.
Grow together.

First: Listen to Liberian business owners and recruit a capable local coordinator.

Next: Test a few paid services and a small training project.

Then: Measure income earned, skills learned, and businesses helped. Expand only when it works.

We want this work to be led by Liberians, with clear records and fair opportunities.

Questions people may ask

Simple answers.

Is this a business or a charity?

Both kinds of support are part of the plan. Paying customers would fund business services and wages. A separate, properly managed donation program would fund eligible training and small-business support.

Can I get a job or training now?

Not yet. We are planning the first pilot. No jobs or training places have been promised.

Can I get money to start a business?

Not yet. We hope to offer small grants, equipment, or mentoring in the future. Any support will need clear rules and available funding.

Will all businesses have to pay?

Businesses that can afford services would pay. Donations could help eligible small businesses receive subsidized support.

Who will run it?

We want strong Liberian leadership and local decision-making. The team and legal structure are still being developed.
